sk-dar.name: Üsküdar
sk-dar.summary: A district on the Asian shore of Istanbul, a conservative cultural center since Ottoman times and site of the Selimiye Barracks.

ey-psultan.name: Eyüp
ey-psultan.summary: A district and historic neighborhood of Istanbul at the head of the Golden Horn, important to Turkish Muslims as the site of the tomb of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, a companion of Muhammad.

service-la-russe.name: Service à la russe
service-la-russe.summary: A style of serving meals course by course to each guest individually, developed in France in the 19th century from Russian table customs, which gradually replaced service à la française.

service-la-fran-aise.name: Service à la française
service-la-fran-aise.summary: A style of serving a meal with all dishes set out at once for diners to help themselves, the norm from the Middle Ages to the 19th century, later largely replaced by service à la russe.

tulum-cheese.name: Tulum peyniri
tulum-cheese.summary: A traditional Turkish goat's milk cheese ripened in a goatskin casing, from which it takes its name.

ihlamur-pavilion.name: Ihlamur Pavilion
ihlamur-pavilion.summary: A former Ottoman imperial summer pavilion in Istanbul, built during the reign of Sultan Abdülmecid I (1839–1860) and now run by Turkey's National Palaces administration.

abd-lmecid-i.name: Abdülmecid I
abd-lmecid-i.summary: 31st sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1839–1861) whose Tanzimat Edict launched an era of reform and closer ties with Britain and France, including alliance in the Crimean War.

gaziantep.name: Gaziantep
gaziantep.summary: A major city in south-central Turkey, historically called Aintab, today famous for kebabs and desserts such as baklava and künefe.

ottoman-baroque-architecture.name: Ottoman Baroque architecture
ottoman-baroque-architecture.summary: An 18th- and early 19th-century Ottoman architectural style influenced by European Baroque, begun under Mahmud I with the Nuruosmaniye Mosque of 1755.

tanzimat.name: Tanzimat
tanzimat.summary: A period of reforms in the Ottoman Empire from 1839 to 1876 that modernized legal, military and administrative systems.

dolmabah-e-clock-tower.name: Dolmabahçe Clock Tower
dolmabah-e-clock-tower.summary: Clock tower outside Dolmabahçe Palace in Istanbul, ordered by Sultan Abdülhamid II and designed by court architect Sarkis Balyan, built between 1890 and 1895.

abdul-hamid-ii.name: Abdul Hamid II
abdul-hamid-ii.summary: 34th sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1876–1909), the last to hold effective control over the fracturing state, who suspended the constitution in 1878 and ruled with absolute power.

raimondo-d-aronco.name: Raimondo D'Aronco
raimondo-d-aronco.summary: Italian Art Nouveau architect (1857–1932) who served as chief palace architect to Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II in Istanbul for 16 years.

osman-hamdi-bey.name: Osman Hamdi Bey
osman-hamdi-bey.summary: Ottoman administrator, intellectual and pioneering painter (1842 to 1910), regarded as the founding father of archaeology, museology and fine arts education in Turkey.

orientalism.name: Orientalism
orientalism.summary: The depiction of the Eastern world by Western artists and writers, later reinterpreted since Edward Said's 1978 book as a patronizing Western attitude toward Asian and North African societies.

dolmabah-e-palace.name: Dolmabahçe Palace
dolmabah-e-palace.summary: 19th-century imperial palace on Istanbul's Bosphorus shore, the main administrative centre of the Ottoman Empire from 1853 to 1887 and 1909 to 1922.

balyan-family.name: Balyan family
balyan-family.summary: An Armenian family of court architects who served Ottoman sultans across five generations in the 18th and 19th centuries, designing palaces, mosques and other major buildings mostly in Constantinople.

hereke.name: Hereke
hereke.summary: A town near İzmit in Turkey, famous for the fine Hereke carpets woven there.

jacquard-machine.name: Jacquard machine
jacquard-machine.summary: A device fitted to a loom, patented in 1804, that automated the weaving of complex patterned textiles using chains of punched cards; it later inspired Babbage's Analytical Engine.

trompe-l-il.name: Trompe-l'œil
trompe-l-il.summary: An artistic technique, mostly used in painting, that creates a highly realistic optical illusion of three-dimensional space and objects on a flat surface.

ortak-y-mosque.name: Ortaköy Mosque
ortak-y-mosque.summary: A mosque on the Bosphorus shore in Istanbul, commissioned by Ottoman Sultan Abdülmecid I and completed around 1854 to 1856.

nusretiye-mosque.name: Nusretiye Mosque
nusretiye-mosque.summary: An ornate mosque in Istanbul's Tophane district, built between 1823 and 1826 for Sultan Mahmud II.

mahmud-ii.name: Mahmud II
mahmud-ii.summary: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1808 to 1839 who abolished the conservative Janissary Corps and pushed major reforms, though the empire kept losing territory.

giuseppe-donizetti.name: Giuseppe Donizetti (Donizetti Pasha)
giuseppe-donizetti.summary: An Italian composer (1788–1856) who led Ottoman imperial military music from 1828, introduced European-style bands, and is believed to have written the first Ottoman national anthem.

hammamizade-i-smail-dede-efendi.name: Ismail Dede Efendi
hammamizade-i-smail-dede-efendi.summary: A composer of Ottoman classical music who lived from 1778 to 1846.

sirkeci-railway-station.name: Sirkeci Railway Station
sirkeci-railway-station.summary: A railway terminal in Istanbul built in 1890 as the eastern terminus of the Orient Express, which ran between Paris and Istanbul from 1883 to 2009.

pertevniyal-valide-sultan-mosque.name: Pertevniyal Valide Sultan Mosque
pertevniyal-valide-sultan-mosque.summary: A grand Ottoman imperial mosque in Istanbul's Aksaray district, built on the order of Sultana Pertevniyal in the 1870s and still drawing thousands of worshippers for Friday prayers.

fatih-mosque-istanbul.name: Fatih Mosque
fatih-mosque-istanbul.summary: An Ottoman mosque in Istanbul built between 1463 and 1470 on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles, named for Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror and rebuilt after a 1766 earthquake.

selimiye-barracks.name: Selimiye Barracks
selimiye-barracks.summary: An Ottoman army barracks in Üsküdar, on Istanbul's Asian side, built in 1800 by Sultan Selim III for his new-model soldiers; it still serves as a Turkish army headquarters.

janissary.name: Janissaries
janissary.summary: Elite Ottoman infantry corps, among the first standing armies equipped mainly with firearms, recruited as boys from Christian families and converted to Islam; the corps was disbanded in 1826.

ra-an-palace.name: Çırağan Palace
ra-an-palace.summary: A former Ottoman palace on the Bosporus in Istanbul, now a hotel; built in 1872, it was gutted by fire in 1910 and its surviving façade later became part of the hotel.

ayazma-mosque.name: Ayazma Mosque
ayazma-mosque.summary: A mosque overlooking the Bosphorus in Üsküdar, Istanbul, commissioned by Ottoman Sultan Mustafa III and built between 1757 and 1761 in the Ottoman Baroque style.

grisaille.name: Grisaille
grisaille.summary: A painting technique using only shades of grey or black, often used to imitate sculpture or as an underpainting before adding colour.

italo-turkish-war.name: Italo-Turkish War
italo-turkish-war.summary: An 1911–1912 war between the Kingdom of Italy and the Ottoman Empire, after which Italy took Libya and the Dodecanese islands; seen as a precursor to World War I.

dodecanese.name: Dodecanese
dodecanese.summary: A group of Greek islands in the southeastern Aegean Sea off the coast of Anatolia, with Rhodes as the dominant island since antiquity.

balkan-wars.name: Balkan Wars
balkan-wars.summary: Two 1912-13 conflicts in which Greece, Serbia, Montenegro and Bulgaria first defeated the Ottoman Empire together, then Bulgaria fought its former allies plus Romania; set the stage for the First World War.

greek-war-of-independence.name: Greek War of Independence
greek-war-of-independence.summary: A war fought from 1821 to 1829 in which Greek revolutionaries won independence from the Ottoman Empire, later aided by Britain, France and Russia.

treaty-of-adrianople-1829.name: Treaty of Adrianople
treaty-of-adrianople-1829.summary: Ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1828–29, giving Russia new Black Sea territory and access to the Danube mouths, and opening the Dardanelles to all commercial ships.

shahada.name: Shahada
shahada.summary: An Islamic declaration of faith and one of the Five Pillars of Islam, stating there is no god but God and Muhammad is His messenger. A single sincere recitation is enough to become a Muslim.

cretan-revolt-1897-1898.name: Cretan Revolt (1897–1898)
cretan-revolt-1897-1898.summary: A successful uprising by Crete's Greek Orthodox population against Ottoman rule, ending in 1898 when the Great Powers made Crete an autonomous state under nominal Ottoman sovereignty.

thessaly.name: Thessaly
thessaly.summary: A geographic and administrative region of northern central Greece, formerly known as Aeolia, which became part of the modern Greek state in 1881.

ibrahim-pasha-of-egypt.name: Ibrahim Pasha
ibrahim-pasha-of-egypt.summary: An Egyptian general and the eldest son of Muhammad Ali, who commanded Egyptian and Ottoman armies and briefly ruled Egypt and Sudan as regent before dying only four months later, in 1848.

diwan-poetry.name: Diwan (poetry)
diwan-poetry.summary: Tradition of poetry collections by a single author across Islamic cultures of West and Central Asia, North Africa and South Asia, dominated by lyric forms such as ghazals.

dadalo-lu.name: Dadaloğlu
dadalo-lu.summary: Turkish Ottoman folk poet-singer, or ozan, of around 1785–1868.

i-brahim-inasi.name: İbrahim Şinasi
i-brahim-inasi.summary: An Ottoman intellectual, journalist and playwright (1826–1871) who founded Turkish dramaturgy, wrote one of the earliest Ottoman plays, and promoted European Enlightenment ideas during the Tanzimat period.

nam-k-kemal.name: Namık Kemal
nam-k-kemal.summary: Ottoman writer, poet and reformer (1840–1888) whose activism helped shape the Young Ottoman movement and pushed toward the Ottoman Empire's first constitutional era in 1876.

ahmet-mithat.name: Ahmet Mithat
ahmet-mithat.summary: Ottoman Turkish journalist, author, translator and publisher of the Tanzimat period who wrote over 250 works and introduced Russian writers such as Tolstoy and Pushkin to Turkish readers.

gen-kalemler.name: Genç Kalemler
gen-kalemler.summary: An Ottoman literary and cultural magazine published 1911-1912, one of the earliest nationalist publications in the empire and the first to call for a national language.

ziya-g-kalp.name: Ziya Gökalp
ziya-g-kalp.summary: Turkish sociologist, writer and politician (1876-1924) who rejected Ottomanism and Islamism for Turkish nationalism, shaping the reforms of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk and modern Kemalism.

mer-seyfettin.name: Ömer Seyfettin
mer-seyfettin.summary: Turkish writer (1884–1920) considered one of the greatest modern Turkish authors, praised for simplifying Turkish by reducing its Persian and Arabic vocabulary.

ali-canip-y-ntem.name: Ali Canip Yöntem
ali-canip-y-ntem.summary: Turkish poet, writer, literary history researcher and politician, born in Istanbul in 1887 and died there in 1967.

ottoman-turkish.name: Ottoman Turkish
ottoman-turkish.summary: The standardized Turkish language register used in the Ottoman Empire from the 14th to 20th centuries, borrowing heavily from Persian and Arabic and largely unintelligible to rural Turks.

persian-alphabet.name: Perso-Arabic script
persian-alphabet.summary: The right-to-left alphabet used to write Persian, essentially the Arabic alphabet plus four extra letters; it also became the basis for other scripts across Central and South Asia.

saj.name: Saj' (sec')
saj.summary: A form of rhymed prose built on end-rhyme and parallelism, the earliest artistic speech style in Arabic, later carried into Ottoman literary use.

ba-lama.name: Bağlama
ba-lama.summary: A long-necked fretted lute used in Turkish and neighboring folk music, closely associated with wandering poet-musicians known as âşıks.

alevism.name: Alevism
alevism.summary: A syncretic, mystic movement mainly in Turkey, linked to a Sufi form of Twelver Shi'ism with Central Asian shamanic elements, historically tied to the Bektashi order founded by Haji Bektash Veli.

imperial-arsenal.name: Tersâne-i Âmire
imperial-arsenal.summary: Main naval shipyard and base of the Ottoman Empire, located on the Golden Horn in Constantinople, active from the 16th century until the empire's end.

golden-horn.name: Golden Horn
golden-horn.summary: Major waterway and inlet of the Bosphorus in Istanbul, forming a sheltered harbor used by Greek, Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman trade for millennia.

ludvig-nobel.name: Ludvig Nobel
ludvig-nobel.summary: Swedish-Russian engineer and businessman (1831–1888), older brother of Alfred Nobel. He is credited with creating the Russian oil industry and was one of the world's richest men.

vladimir-shukhov.name: Vladimir Shukhov
vladimir-shukhov.summary: Russian and Soviet engineer, scientist and architect (1853 to 1939), famed for pioneering the world's first hyperboloid structures. He also invented the first cracking method used in oil refining.

branobel.name: Branobel
branobel.summary: Oil company set up in Russia by the Nobel family and the baron Peter von Bilderling, working mainly in Baku and also in Cheleken. It became one of the world's largest oil companies in the late 19th century.

dmitri-mendeleev.name: Dmitri Mendeleev
dmitri-mendeleev.summary: Russian chemist (1834-1907) known for formulating the periodic law and creating a version of the periodic table. He used it to predict three undiscovered elements; mendelevium is named for him.

national-botanical-garden-of-georgia.name: Tiflis Botanical Garden
national-botanical-garden-of-georgia.summary: Botanical garden in Tbilisi, Georgia, now the National Botanical Garden of Georgia. It began as royal gardens described in 1671 and covers 161 hectares with over 4,500 taxonomic groups.

abdulaziz.name: Abdulaziz
abdulaziz.summary: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1861 to 1876, the first to travel to Western Europe as sultan, overthrown in a coup in 1876 amid economic crisis and unrest.

chemins-de-fer-ottomans-d-anatolie.name: Anatolian Railway
chemins-de-fer-ottomans-d-anatolie.summary: An Ottoman railway company founded in 1888, the busiest line in the empire, linking Istanbul to Ankara and Konya; it was financed by Germany's Deutsche Bank.

robert-nobel.name: Robert Nobel
robert-nobel.summary: Swedish businessman and industrialist (1829–1896), founder of Branobel and a pioneer of the Russian oil industry.

alexander-mantashev.name: Alexander Mantashev
alexander-mantashev.summary: Russian oil magnate, industrialist and philanthropist of Armenian origin (1842–1911). By the end of his life he was one of the world's wealthiest individuals.

baku-batumi-pipeline.name: Baku–Batumi pipeline
baku-batumi-pipeline.summary: Name for several pipeline projects carrying kerosene and crude oil from the Caspian region to Batumi on the Black Sea. When built in 1906, it was the world's longest kerosene pipeline.

derince.name: Derince
derince.summary: Seaport, municipality and district of Kocaeli Province, Turkey, with about 146,000 people in 2022. Its port is one of the few in Turkey under government control, run by the state railways.

auspicious-incident.name: Auspicious Incident
auspicious-incident.summary: The forced disbandment of the centuries-old janissary corps by Ottoman Sultan Mahmud II on 15 June 1826, after which thousands of janissaries were executed, exiled or imprisoned.

crimean-war.name: Crimean War
crimean-war.summary: A war fought from 1853 to 1856 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, France, Britain and Sardinia, centred on the siege of the Russian naval base at Sevastopol.

heraclius-ii-of-georgia.name: Heraclius II
heraclius-ii-of-georgia.summary: King of Kakheti from 1744 and of the united Kartli-Kakheti from 1762 to 1798, in eastern Georgia; he unified the region and placed it under Russian protection in 1783.

kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti.name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti
kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti.summary: A united eastern Georgian kingdom formed in 1762 from Kartli and Kakheti under the Bagrationi dynasty; it became a Russian protectorate in 1783 and was annexed by Russia in 1801.

georgian-governorate.name: Georgian Governorate
georgian-governorate.summary: An administrative division of the Caucasus Viceroyalty of the Russian Empire, centered on Tiflis (Tbilisi), established in 1801 after Russia annexed the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti.

kingdom-of-imereti.name: Kingdom of Imereti
kingdom-of-imereti.summary: A western Georgian kingdom established in 1463 by the Bagrationi royal family, contested for centuries between Georgian, Ottoman and Russian power before Russia annexed it in 1810.

ottoman-public-debt-administration.name: Ottoman Public Debt Administration
ottoman-public-debt-administration.summary: European-run body set up in 1881 to collect Ottoman debts owed to foreign creditors, growing into a bureaucracy of thousands that financed railways and other projects.

ottoman-reform-edict-of-1856.name: Imperial Reform Edict
ottoman-reform-edict-of-1856.summary: An 1856 edict of Sultan Abdulmejid I promising equality in education, government appointments and justice to all Ottoman subjects regardless of religion, issued after the Crimean War.

edict-of-g-lhane.name: Edict of Gülhane
edict-of-g-lhane.summary: An 1839 proclamation by Ottoman Sultan Abdülmecid I launching the Tanzimat reforms, promising abolition of tax farming, conscription reform, and equal rights for all Ottoman subjects.

young-ottomans.name: Young Ottomans
young-ottomans.summary: A secret society founded in 1865 by Ottoman intellectuals dissatisfied with the Tanzimat reforms, seeking a constitutional government still rooted in Islam.

first-constitutional-era.name: First Constitutional Era
first-constitutional-era.summary: Period of constitutional monarchy in the Ottoman Empire from 1876 to 1878, ended when Sultan Abdul Hamid II suspended parliament and restored absolute rule.

grand-vizier.name: Grand vizier
grand-vizier.summary: The title of the effective head of government in many Islamic states, first held under the Abbasid Caliphate and later by the Ottoman, Mughal and other empires.

hamidian-massacres.name: Hamidian massacres
hamidian-massacres.summary: Massacres of Armenians, and in some cases Assyrians, in the Ottoman Empire in the mid-1890s, named after Sultan Abdul Hamid II, killing an estimated 100,000 to 300,000 people.

qajar-iran.name: Qajar Iran
qajar-iran.summary: The Iranian state ruled by the Qajar dynasty from 1789 to 1925, founded by Agha Mohammad Khan, which faced major challenges to its sovereignty from Russia and Britain during the Great Game.

treaty-of-gulistan.name: Treaty of Gulistan
treaty-of-gulistan.summary: An 1813 treaty drafted by British mediator Sir Gore Ouseley, following the Russian storming of Lankaran; it later contributed to a fresh Russo-Persian war in 1826.

treaty-of-turkmenchay.name: Treaty of Turkmenchay
treaty-of-turkmenchay.summary: 1828 treaty ending the Russo-Persian War of 1826 to 1828, forcing Qajar Iran to cede the Erivan, Nakhchivan and Talysh khanates in the South Caucasus to Russia.

anatolia-eyalet.name: Anatolia Eyalet
anatolia-eyalet.summary: One of the two core provinces of the early Ottoman Empire, established in 1393 with its capital eventually moved to Kütahya, and dissolved around 1841 during the Tanzimat reforms.

armenian-revolutionary-federation.name: Dashnaks
armenian-revolutionary-federation.summary: Members of the Armenian Revolutionary Federation, a nationalist and socialist political party founded in 1890, long influential in the Armenian diaspora.

ottoman-bank.name: Ottoman Bank
ottoman-bank.summary: Bank chartered in 1856 that became the dominant financial institution in the Ottoman Empire, lending to its government and issuing its banknotes.

sublime-porte.name: Sublime Porte
sublime-porte.summary: A term for the central government of the Ottoman Empire in Istanbul, referring to the building that housed the Grand Vizier's office and other key ministries.

pavel-tsitsianov.name: Pavel Tsitsianov
pavel-tsitsianov.summary: A Russian general of Georgian noble origin who led Russia's conquest of the South Caucasus as commander-in-chief there from 1802 until his assassination near Baku in 1806.

ganja-azerbaijan.name: Ganja
ganja-azerbaijan.summary: Azerbaijan's third-largest city, historically also known by the Armenian name Gandzak, and capital of the Ganja Khanate until Russia annexed it in 1813.

principality-of-mingrelia.name: Mingrelia
principality-of-mingrelia.summary: A historical Georgian state, also known as Odishi or Samegrelo, ruled by the Dadiani dynasty.

principality-of-guria.name: Principality of Guria
principality-of-guria.summary: A historical state in southwestern Georgia ruled by twenty-two princes of the House of Gurieli from the 1460s until Russia annexed it in 1829.

svaneti.name: Svaneti
svaneti.summary: A mountainous province in northwestern Georgia along the Greater Caucasus range, home to the Svans, an ethnic subgroup of Georgians.

millet-ottoman-empire.name: Millet
millet-ottoman-empire.summary: In the Ottoman Empire, an autonomous legal community allowing non-Muslim religious groups to govern themselves under their own laws, later used from the 19th century for protected ethnic minority groups.

miletus.name: Miletus
miletus.summary: Ancient Greek city on Anatolia's western coast, a wealthy maritime and trading power that founded dozens of Mediterranean and Black Sea colonies and was home to early philosophers such as Thales; known in Hittite records as Millawata.

ionian-school-philosophy.name: Milesian school
ionian-school-philosophy.summary: The group of early Ionian philosophers—Thales, Anaximander, and Anaximenes—based in Miletus, who sought nature's basic underlying element through abstract reasoning rather than experiment.

thales-of-miletus.name: Thales of Miletus
thales-of-miletus.summary: A pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from Miletus, c. 626-548 BC, often called the first philosopher for explaining nature without myth; he held that everything derives from water.

anaximander.name: Anaximander
anaximander.summary: Pre-Socratic Greek philosopher of Miletus (c. 610–c. 546 BC), the first known to write down his studies, who proposed the apeiron as the source of all things and created an early map of the world.

anaximenes-of-miletus.name: Anaximenes
anaximenes-of-miletus.summary: A pre-Socratic Greek philosopher from Miletus (c. 586/585–526/525 BC), the last of the three Milesian School thinkers, who held that air was the basic element from which all things form.

mehmed-i.name: Mehmed I
mehmed-i.summary: Ottoman sultan (r. 1413–1421) who reunified the empire after a civil war among Bayezid I's sons and restored central Ottoman authority.

syriac-catholic-church.name: Syriac Catholic Church
syriac-catholic-church.summary: An Eastern Catholic church in full communion with Rome, based mainly in Syria and Iraq, tracing its origins to the ancient Church of Antioch.

chaldean-catholic-church.name: Chaldean Catholic Church
chaldean-catholic-church.summary: An Eastern Catholic church descended from the Church of the East, formed through a 1552 schism and led today by the Patriarch of Baghdad, with about 617,000 members worldwide.

syriac-orthodox-church.name: Syriac Orthodox Church
syriac-orthodox-church.summary: An Oriental Orthodox church, also known as the Jacobite Church, tracing its origins to the ancient Church of Antioch and led by the Patriarch of Antioch.

armenian-patriarchate-of-constantinople.name: Armenian Patriarch of Constantinople
armenian-patriarchate-of-constantinople.summary: Head of the Armenian Patriarchate of Constantinople, an autonomous see of the Armenian Apostolic Church with significant historical political and spiritual authority in the Ottoman Empire.

market-gate-of-miletus.name: Market Gate of Miletus
market-gate-of-miletus.summary: Large 2nd-century AD marble monument from Miletus, excavated and rebuilt by German archaeologists in the early 1900s and now displayed, reconstructed from fragments, in Berlin's Pergamon Museum.

pergamon-museum.name: Pergamon Museum
pergamon-museum.summary: A museum on Berlin's Museum Island, built from 1910 to 1930, holding major antiquities such as the reconstructed Ishtar Gate, closed since 2023 for renovation.

didim.name: Didim
didim.summary: Seaside resort town in Aydın Province, Turkey, with about 97,000 residents in 2022, built on the site of the ancient city of Didyma and its ruined Temple of Apollo.

be-ikta-j-k.name: Beşiktaş Gymnastics Club
be-ikta-j-k.summary: A Turkish sports club founded in 1903, based in Istanbul, whose football team is one of Turkey's 'Big Three' and has never been relegated.

galatasaray-s-k.name: Galatasaray Sports Club
galatasaray-s-k.summary: A major Turkish sports club in Istanbul founded in 1905, whose football team holds the most league and cup titles in Turkey and won the 2000 UEFA Cup and Super Cup.

fenerbah-e-s-k.name: Fenerbahçe S.K.
fenerbah-e-s-k.summary: Turkish multi-sport club based in Istanbul, founded in 1907, one of the country's oldest and most successful clubs with titles across many sports.

tophane-clock-tower.name: Tophane Clock Tower
tophane-clock-tower.summary: Clock tower in Bursa, Turkey, six floors and 33 metres tall, built in 1904–1905 on the site of an earlier tower and now used as a fire lookout.

beyo-lu.name: Beyoğlu
beyo-lu.summary: A district on the European side of Istanbul, historically known as Pera, which grew as a Genoese colony in the Middle Ages.

i-ek-pasaj.name: Çiçek Pasajı
i-ek-pasaj.summary: A historic covered arcade on İstiklal Avenue in Istanbul's Beyoğlu district, lined with cafes, winehouses and restaurants; originally built as the Cité de Péra.

oil-wrestling.name: Oil wrestling
oil-wrestling.summary: The national sport of Turkey, in which oiled wrestlers try to win by gripping their opponent's leather pants, with roots tracing back to ancient Egypt and Assyria.

turkish-archery.name: Turkish archery
turkish-archery.summary: A traditional form of archery fully developed under the Ottoman Empire, with roots in the Eurasian Steppe dating to the second millennium BC; recognized by UNESCO in 2019.

jereed.name: Jereed
jereed.summary: A traditional Turkish team sport on horseback in which riders score points by throwing a blunt wooden javelin at opposing horsemen; it originated among Central Asian Turkic peoples and reached Anatolia in the 11th century.

kar-yaka-s-k.name: Karşıyaka Sports Club
kar-yaka-s-k.summary: Turkey's oldest sports club and the first founded in Anatolia, established in İzmir in 1912, fielding football, basketball and other teams.

altay-s-k.name: Altay Sports Club
altay-s-k.summary: Turkish football club based in İzmir, formed in 1914 and nicknamed Büyük Altay (Great Altay).

lk-spor.name: Ülküspor
lk-spor.summary: A Turkish football club from İzmir founded in 1914 as Turkish Fatherland Football Club, the third club formed in the city after Altay and Karşıyaka.

bulgarian-exarchate.name: Bulgarian Exarchate
bulgarian-exarchate.summary: Official name of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church from its establishment by Ottoman decree in 1870/1872 until 1945, declared schismatic by the Patriarchate of Constantinople and central to forming the modern Bulgarian nation.

ecumenical-patriarchate-of-constantinopl.name: Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople
ecumenical-patriarchate-of-constantinopl.summary: One of the autocephalous churches of Eastern Orthodox Christianity, based in Constantinople and regarded as the mother church of most modern Eastern Orthodox churches.
